findings.explanation: Audit policy namespaces entries are exact string matches (no wildcard), and cluster-scoped objects such as clusterrolebindings, clusterroles and certificatesigningrequests carry an empty namespace. With namespaces: ["*"] and no catch-all rule, these RBAC and CSR mutations are not audited at all, so the detection is blind.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the namespaces field from the RBAC and CSR rules (an empty list matches every namespace, including the empty one for cluster-scoped resources) and end the policy with a catch-all '- level: Metadata' rule, as the guide's policy does.

findings.explanation: The entries are templated and miss the predictable benign sources for this search. Detailed Case 10 and Case 11 already name some of them.
findings.quote: Batch `count` on `kube:apiserver:audit`** — Scheduled automation elevates `cluster` without crossing `resp_code` >= 200
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: kube-controller-manager's csrapproving controller (system:serviceaccount:kube-system:certificate-controller) auto-approving kubelet client and serving CSRs on every rotation; ArgoCD or Flux re-applying the same binding; kubeadm, eksctl or managed-service bootstrap creating initial cluster-admin bindings; operators installing ClusterRoles with pods/exec or wildcard rules (for example monitoring or backup agents). Say how to recognise each (actor, user agent, cluster age, git commit).

findings.explanation: RBAC binding and ClusterRole mutations are change events (the guide maps kube:apiserver:audit to Change), not authentication events. Authentication is only used for an unrelated per-user login count, and the cimSpl does not reproduce the detection.
findings.suggested_fix: List Change as the primary model (All_Changes with object_category for the RBAC resource and action created/modified). Describe the Authentication join as optional context only, or drop it.

findings.explanation: The text says the fenced SPL 'must match the spl JSON field byte-for-byte', but the fenced copy builds subject_key with strcat() while the spl field uses '.' concatenation. The savedsearches.conf sketch also sets dispatch.latest_time = now, while the SPL hard-codes latest=@h.
findings.suggested_fix: Paste the exact spl field into the fence and align dispatch.latest_time with the SPL's @h snap (or drop the inline time bounds).

findings.explanation: The URL is the access-control index page, not the auditing page. 'T1078.004 Cloud Accounts (Containers)' adds a qualifier that is not part of the ATT&CK technique name, and 'Splunk — Add-on for Kubernetes' labels a Helm chart as an add-on.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug/debug-cluster/audit/, title the MITRE entry 'T1078.004 Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts', and link the splunk-otel-collector-chart repository or Splunkbase 6790 instead of the add-on page.

findings.explanation: Following the documented audit policy yields no RBAC audit events, which any end-to-end verification would have exposed; the reviewer is a generic repository handle.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft until the policy and search have been exercised in a lab and signed off by a named reviewer.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: masters_g matches 'system:masters' anywhere in the lower-cased _raw, including the actor's own user.groups. Any cluster-admin-tier binding change made by a super-admin certificate user (whose groups include system:masters) is labelled rbac_group_system_masters_binding and paged as critical even when no subject references system:masters. Test requestObject.subjects{}.name instead of _raw.

The rex for system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name> over _raw captures the actor's username when the actor is a service account. RBAC subjects of kind ServiceAccount are serialized as {kind, name, namespace}, not as system:serviceaccount strings, so subject_key usually identifies who made the change rather than who received cluster-admin, and allowlist joins key on the wrong principal. Extract requestObject.subjects{}.kind, name and namespace instead.
resp_code defaults to 201 when responseStatus.code is missing, so events without a response status (for example non-ResponseComplete stages or truncated records) are treated as successful mutations.
Granting cluster-admin or escalating ClusterRole rules maps directly to T1098.006 Account Manipulation: Additional Container Cluster Roles. Only T1078.004 is listed.

summary: The UC has a strong, well-scoped design for auditing the cluster-admin tier (cluster-admin bindings, system:masters, escalating ClusterRole rules, CSR approvals) and a useful break-glass allowlist. But the audit policy it tells readers to deploy would never log the cluster-scoped RBAC objects it depends on. The raw-text matching also misattributes system:masters and service-account subjects, and the false-positive and CIM sections are generic.
